chunks: Ḥukaym ibn Dāwūd ibn Ḥukaym narrated to me from Salamah ibn Khaťťāb, who said:

‘Amr ibn Sa‘īd said: Walīd ibn Ghassān narrated to me from someone who narrated to him, who said: The Jinn used to weep over al-Ḥusayn ibn ‘Alī (peace be upon him), saying: To whom do these houses in al-Ṭaff belong, the houses which were built unwillingly? These are the houses of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him), they reciprocate each other’s weeping.

key_terms.الطَّفِّ: Al-Tabb, a region in Iraq near Karbala associated with Imam al-Husayn
key_terms.الْجِنُّ: The Jinn, a spiritual creation in Islamic cosmology

ai.seo_question: What do the Jinn say about the houses of Imam al-Husain in al-Tabb?
ai.summary: This narration from Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat* highlights the cosmic scale of the Karbala tragedy, illustrating that the lamentation for Imam al-Ḥusayn (a.s.) transcends the human realm to include the Jinn, who recite poetry identifying the structures in al-Ṭaff as his unwillingly built houses. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the universal resonance of the Imam’s sacrifice, where even unseen creatures participate in mourning the Ahl al-Bayt. The 'echoing lamentation' serves as a perpetual spiritual reminder of the injustice suffered, reinforcing the concept of *Nahj al-Balagha* in nature itself.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 4. Ḥukaym ibn Dāwūd ibn Ḥukaym narrated to me from Salamah ibn Khaťťāb,

from ‘Amr ibn Sa’īd, from Walīd ibn Ghassān, from someone who narrated to him, who said: The Jinn used to weep over Ḥusain (a.s.) and recite the following poem: To whom do these houses in Ťaf belong, the houses which were built unwillingly? These are the houses of Ḥusain (a.s.) and they reciprocate each other’s weeping (over Ḥusain (a.s.)).
